rv.q: Under the direction of Jeffrey Cass, this ensemble of 16, plus an amazing orchestra conducted by Phil Videckis, brings Schwartz' fantasy to new life.
BrightSide's presentation is a dazzling and absolutely delightful production that offers both a polished playfulness and a thought-provoking punch.
I love the show Pippin and the BrightSide Theatre in Naperville added a layer of quaint suburban charm to this classic piece.
BrightSide’s production is worth seeing, and “Pippin” could be revived more often (another production will be at Skokie Theatre in September).
This is a spectacular, not-to-be-missed, finale show for Brightside's thirteenth season.
